stores.title: How this is read
stores.p1: One row per store, summed from Stock Visibility's stock rows at storage location 0001. Stock is the till-side counter: SAP's counter less the till sales SAP has not posted yet. SAP stock is SAP's own counter, and the gap is SAP stock less till-side stock — sold at the till, not in SAP yet.
stores.p2: Held is every hold not released, in two parts: standing holds, and holds sold at the till whose sale is not applied to the counter yet (sold not applied).
stores.p3: Reserved is the reserved recompute's total for the store. If the recompute has never run it says "not computed", never zero. If its last success is older than 15 minutes it is marked stale, with its time.
stores.p4: Free is till-side stock less held less reserved, not floored at zero. While reserved is not computed, free is till-side stock less held and says "reserved not included". Every figure is a sum across items, in base units.
stores.p5: The status is the worst of the store's flags: no SAP document for over 24 hours, a standing hold older than 2 days, a sale not applied for over 2 hours, items below zero, a differing nightly comparison, stock on placeholder batches. Each is a Watch, except over 500 items below zero, or any item below zero or a differing comparison in a store in Blocking, which are a Problem. The list is a copy at most a minute old; Refresh reads it again.

store.title: How this is read
store.p1: The header is read fresh from Stock Visibility each time this page opens, never the stores list's minute-old copy. Its figures are the same sums as the store's row on the list: stock rows at storage location 0001, in base units.
store.p2: The last SAP document applied is where the SAP feed stands for this store; the last till read is where the till feed stands. Each shows its last attempt beside it, so a feed that tries and fails shows.
store.p3: The lists below read nothing until you search. Search with empty boxes lists the whole view, 25 rows a page. Refresh reads the open tab again, and only it.

items.title: How this is read
items.p1: One row per item with a stock row at this store, from Stock Visibility, at storage location 0001. The item box takes an item number, or two characters or more of a name: a name is looked up in HQ's item master, and the numbers found are searched. Over 200 items for one name is refused; type more of it.
items.p2: A batch in the batch box narrows the items to those holding that batch here — our batch exactly, or the vendor batch; a prefix of three characters or more ending in * is allowed.
items.p3: SAP stock, till-side stock, the gap, held, reserved and free are read as on the store's header, for this item. Names come from HQ's item master, in your language; an item the master does not know has no name.

batches.title: How this is read
batches.p1: One row per item and batch at this store, from Stock Visibility, sorted by item and then expiry. The vendor batch is matched by its key, upper case and trimmed.
batches.p2: Free for the take door is the batch's till-side stock less the holds on that batch; reserved is not taken off, because the take door works batch by batch. A batch has no last-update time, so the day it was first received is shown instead.
batches.p3: A placeholder batch is marked by Stock Visibility's own placeholder rule. Expired means the expiry day is before today; within 90 days means today or one of the next 90 days.

holds.title: How this is read
holds.p1: One row per hold at this store, from Stock Visibility's hold ledger. By default the list shows the holds that count in the held figure: standing holds, and holds sold at the till whose sale is not applied to the counter yet. Released holds of the last 7 days are listed on request, with when and why they were released.
holds.p2: Oldest first, so the stuck ones are on top. The age is from the time the hold was taken to when this page was read; for a released hold, to its release.
holds.p3: A hold shows its picking document and line, or its till sale (store and transaction), as Stock Visibility holds them. Nothing is joined from OMS: no customer order number, no customer, no patient.

takes.title: How this is read
takes.p1: The take door's calls for this store on one day — today unless you pick another. Each is granted (with the batches it took, from its holds), refused (with its reason, and the batch the door named) or failed (with its status and how long it took).
takes.p2: A failed call carries no item: the request log holds only the store and the take id. So failed calls are listed by store and day, and are left out when you search by item or batch.
takes.p3: The day is written into the address with the search, so a shared link reads the same day.

feeds.title: How this is read
feeds.p1: Read when the tab opens, from the store's own console row. The SAP place is the SAP entry date and time of the last SAP document applied for this store; the till place is where the till feed stands. Each shows its last attempt, so a feed that tries and fails shows.
feeds.p2: The nightly comparison runs for counted stores only (Seeded or Blocking): it counts the batches where our book and SAP's differ. A store not counted has none.

stage.title: How this is read
stage.p1: Read when the tab opens, through the stage screen's own reads, under the console's grant: the store's stage, its stage log (newest first), its last seed run and the gates toward Blocking.
stage.p2: Read-only. Moves are made on Store stages, by those who hold its grant.

fleet.title: How this is read
fleet.p1: Facts that belong to no store, read once when this page opens from Stock Visibility's status routes: each feed's last full pass and its age, the reserved recompute's run, the held-served switch, the hold ledger reader's lag and today's take door figures.
fleet.p2: A fact whose route did not answer — an older Stock Visibility, or one that could not be reached — says "No answer". It is never shown as healthy.
fleet.p3: The facts that are a problem now are also said once, above the stores list, so no store is blamed for them.

item.title: How this is read
item.sapStock: SAP counter: what SAP has posted for this item at storage location 0001 of this store.
item.gap: Sold at the till, not in SAP yet: the SAP counter less the till-side counter — the till sales SAP has not posted.
item.tillStock: Till-side: the SAP counter less the till sales SAP has not posted. It is the store's stock of this item.
item.held: Held: every hold on this item not released — standing, and sold not applied (a sale not yet applied to the counter still counts, as Stock Visibility counts it). Holds on no batch are in it too.
item.reserved: Reserved: the reserved recompute's total for this store and item. Never computed shows no figure, never a zero; stale shows its figure and its time, marked.
item.free: Free: till-side less held less reserved, never floored at zero. When reserved was never computed it is left out, and free says so.
item.answeredNow: Answered now: what the stock read answers the channels for this store and item at this moment, and the rule that made it. Under the live-orders rule the open orders are taken off in place of held.
item.changeFeed: Change feed: the figure the change feed sends — till-side less held less reserved, floored at zero.
item.otherStock: Other stock types: quality, blocked, returns, restricted, in transit and in transfer are not unrestricted, so they are not in the sum. Each is shown when it is not zero.

itemBatches.title: How this is read
itemBatches.p1: The store's batches of this item, by expiry. Free for the take door is a batch's till-side stock less the holds on that batch; reserved is not taken off.

itemHolds.title: How this is read
itemHolds.p1: The item's holds not released (standing, and sold not applied) and those released in the last 7 days, one list, as Stock Visibility holds them. Nothing is joined from OMS.

itemTakes.title: How this is read
itemTakes.p1: The take door's calls for this item today and the two days before. A failed call carries no item, so failed calls are not listed here.

itemStores.title: How this is read
itemStores.p1: The item at every store, from each store's stock row, 25 a page: SAP stock, till-side, held, reserved and free by the stores list's rules. A row opens the item at that store.

find.title: How this is read
find.p1: With a batch, Find asks every store for it — our batch or the vendor batch, with or without an item — and answers one row per store, item and batch, with the count of rows and of stores. A row opens the item at that store.
find.p2: Without a batch, Find answers items from HQ's item master, by number or by name. An item opens its stores on this page.
find.p3: With both boxes empty, Find asks nothing. A GS1 code is read first, and its item and its lot are searched.

sap.title: How this is read
sap.p1: Read live from SAP when you press Read SAP — never on opening the tab — for this store and at most 5 SAP entry days. SAP's material documents are summed by entry day and movement type: documents, lines, and the quantity in and out. SAP user names are not read.
sap.p2: Opening a row reads its lines from SAP, 25 a page, and marks each against our copy of SAP's documents: applied (in our book), received but not applied yet, or not received by us — so a missing document shows here.
sap.p3: Above the list stands where our SAP feed is for this store: the last SAP document applied, and its last attempt. When SAP is not connected on this host, or could not be reached, that is said in its own sentence — an empty list always means SAP has no movement.

movements.title: How this is read
movements.p1: Read from our own ledger when you press Read — never on opening the tab — for this item at this store and at most 7 local days, newest first, 25 a page.
movements.p2: Each line shows the feed it came by (SAP or the till), its movement type and signed quantity, its batch, the document it came from, and what it did to each counter: a SAP sale moves the SAP counter only, a till sale the till-side counter only, a receipt both.
movements.p3: It is not put side by side with SAP's movements: our ledger's times are ours, not SAP's entry days, and the ledger has no index by store. The store's SAP movements tab marks each SAP line against our copy instead.
